key_insight: Small, localized charge deficits can trigger sustained electroconvection at about two thirds of the linear instability threshold.
engineering_relevance: Electrohydrodynamic systems may require charge-fluctuation tolerances to avoid unexpected convection below nominal linear stability limits.
method: Nonlinear non-modal optimization using direct–adjoint electrohydrodynamic equations.
Search for the smallest charge perturbations that trigger convection.
Direct numerical simulations and analysis of the separating edge state.
evidence_signal: The minimum triggering perturbation rises from about 0.5% of injected charge near the linear threshold to 3% at two thirds of it, consistent with direct numerical simulations.
watch_item: The reported thresholds apply to the studied unipolar-injection model; transfer to specific devices requires validation under their operating conditions.
paper_title: Nonlinear non-modal stability and minimal perturbations in electroconvection driven by unipolar injection
